Thought: The final volume from the log file is 6354.1325. The number of atoms is 500. To calculate the density, I will use the formula:

\[
\text{Density} = \frac{\text{Number of atoms} \times \text{Atomic mass of Cu}}{\text{Volume}}
\]

The atomic mass of copper (Cu) is approximately 63.546 g/mol. Since the volume is given in Å³, I need to convert it to cm³ (1 Å³ = 1e-24 cm³) and use Avogadro's number (6.022e23 atoms/mol) for the conversion.

\[
\text{Density} = \frac{500 \times 63.546}{6354.1325 \times 1e-24 \times 6.022e23}
\]

Calculating this will give the density in g/cm³. Let's compute this value.
\[
\text{Density} = \frac{500 \times 63.546}{6354.1325 \times 1e-24 \times 6.022e23} \approx 8.37 \text{ g/cm}^3
\]
